body.heading: A daily crowd of almost-friends
paragraphs: The school gate gathers the same adults at the same time every day, which makes it a small community whether anyone planned it or not. It is also a place of rushing, double-parking, and children at ankle height — fertile ground for both friction and kindness.
The kind acts here are mostly about making space: physical space on the pavement, and social space for the parent who is clearly having the morning from the other place.

body.heading: Small things that change the temperature
paragraphs: Hold the gate. Smile at the child who is dragging their feet rather than tutting at the parent. Let the flustered driver in. If your child mentions a classmate's name often, learn the parent's name too and use it — being known by name at the gate turns a crowd into a circle.
Notice the new family. Starting a school mid-year is exile for adults as much as children; one conversation and an invitation to the class coffee can shorten it by months.

body.heading: Model it where they can see
paragraphs: Children absorb the gate's etiquette by watching ours. The driver you wave thanks to, the lollipop person greeted by name, the patience in the rain — it is all curriculum, delivered at ankle height.
None of this requires being a saint at twenty to nine in the rain. It asks only for the ordinary decencies, done where small witnesses can learn them by heart.

description: The school run gathers the same people daily; a little space, a learned name, and patience make it a kinder crowd.
